title: Transfer higher-direct-image vanishing from cyclic groups to constant module coefficients
statement:
Let $h:Y\to X$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, let $\Lambda$ be an arbitrary commutative ring, and let $d,q\in\mathbf N$. If $R^q h_*\underline{\mathbf Z/e}=0$ as an abelian sheaf for every $e\mid d$, then $R^q h_*\underline{\Lambda/d\Lambda}=0$ as a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules. Divisibility includes $0\mid0$ and $\mathbf Z/0=\mathbf Z$.

proof.text: Express the underlying additive group of Lambda/dLambda as the filtered union of its finitely generated subgroups. The structure theorem AddCommGroup.equiv_free_prod_directSum_zmod (Mathlib.GroupTheory.FiniteAbelian.Basic) writes each as a finite sum of cyclic groups. Every finite cyclic order divides d because d kills the subgroup. A nonzero free part is possible only when d=0, when it consists of copies of Z=ZMod 0 and 0 divides 0. The zero subgroup is the empty finite sum. The structure theorem is the existing Mathlib declaration at Basic.lean:119-132; the additional check is elementary: d kills the generator of Z/e exactly when e divides d, and kills a nonzero free generator only if d=0.

The constant abelian sheaf is the filtered colimit of the constant sheaves of these subgroups. On affine etale U the scheme Y x_X U is qcqs, so cohomology commutes with this filtered colimit by 03Q5. Use 03Q8 and colimit-preserving sheafification to deduce that higher direct images commute with this coefficient colimit. Additivity deals with each finite sum, whose higher direct image is zero by the hypothesis. The colimit is therefore zero.

The underlying constant module sheaf is the constant abelian sheaf of its additive group. Use the natural module/abelian cohomology comparison on every Y x_X U, with its compatibility in U, and the sheafified-presheaf formula to identify underlying module higher direct images with abelian higher direct images (03FD and 03Q8). The comparison node is already proved for Lambda : Type (u+1), exactly the coefficient universe here; no conversion to the smaller-universe SheafOfModules statement is needed. Forgetting reflects zero objects.
